# WO-273: Listing finder: error paths return a reason, never crash a scan
Status: queued (pre-approved: start when a WIP slot frees; note it on BOARD.md first)
Vendor: codex
Agent: test-quality (Hannah Cole)
Owner contact: Morgan Reyes (check-ins via CODEX_TO_CLAUDE.md)
Kind: engine
Target release: 0.4
Source: in-house 0.4 groundwork batch 2026-11-09, CLAUDE-065 (in-house offline until about Nov 14; vendors keep working the queue)
Worktree: `.vendor-wt/wo-273` on `vendor/wo-273` from main
Tracker: issue pending (in-house syncs freemyid-pm)

## Goal
Make `listing_finder.py` survive every failure a fake fetcher can produce: timeout, HTTP 403/429/500, empty body, truncated HTML, wrong encoding, and a selector that no longer matches. Each failure becomes a 'could not check' outcome with a short reason code, not an exception and not a silent 'no listings'.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Table test over the failure kinds above with a fake fetcher; each yields the unchecked outcome and a reason code (no URL, name or page text in the reason).
2. A selector that matches nothing on a page that clearly has a results container is reported as 'layout changed', not 'clean'.
3. One failing broker never stops the others in the same call (test with 3 brokers, the middle one failing).
4. No network: the autouse fixture blocks sockets; fakes only.

This is Codex code-lane work (owner, 2026-11-09): fix and improve the listed module(s) directly, with tests; don't xfail a bug you can fix here. No contract changes: public function signatures, `src/freemyid/models.py`, `interfaces.py`, schema files, `--json` shapes and documented CLI output stay as they are (additive helpers inside the listed files are fine). If the work turns out to need a contract change, stop and say so in VENDOR_STATUS.md "Questions for the owner". Fake data only, offline (fake fetchers, no network), Windows-safe paths in tests (`tmp_path`, `pathlib`, no `/tmp`). Typed, ruff-clean, small diff. Line numbers, where cited, are from main at the time of writing; re-check them.
